MINUTES
  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETINGS
  MONDAY, MAY 5, 2025

1.  CALL TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
by CHAIR OLSON at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chamber.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI led those assembled in the Pledge of Allegiance.

3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Olson, Nicklas, Repp-Loadsman, Romanelli, Schachter, Yoo

  Commissioners Absent:  Medawar

  City Staff Present:  Jeannie Naughton, Community Development Director
  Whitney Berry, Senior Planner
  Carol Corea, Administrative Analyst

4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES, MARCH 3, 2025

COMMISSIONER YOO made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR NICKLAS to,

  APPROVE THE PLANNING COMMISSIONER MEETING MINUTES OF MARCH 3, 2025.

There being no objection, CHAIR OLSON so ordered.

5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

NONE

  APPROVE ITEM 6A

There being no objection, CHAIR OLSON so ordered.

  a 1,419 square foot single-story residential addition, and three Minor Deviations for a single-
  story addition built along existing building lines with legal nonconforming side yard setbacks
  (MD-250085), and a covered front porch that encroaches into the front yard not further than
  the forwardmost building line (MD-250087) and will decrease the required front yard area by
  less than 10% (MD-250088).

Senior Planner Berry stated that after the public notice for the project was issued, an error was

8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION No.: PA-250001; ADDRESS:82 DAPPLEGRAY LANE, ROLLING
  HILLS ESTATES CA 90274; APPLICANT: KELSEY FAIR, FAIR STUDIOS/HRS;
  DESCRIPTION: A request for a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination (NC-250002) for
  rear yard improvements, a Grading Permit (G-250003) for the import of more than 20 cubic
  yards of earth materials for fill greater than three feet in vertical height at its deepest point, a
  Variance to exceed lot coverage by more than 10% (V-250004) and a Variance to allow a
  designated future horse keeping area closer than 35 feet to on- and off-site dwellings (V-
  250081).

Senior Planner Berry provided a presentation for Planning Application No. PA-250001 summarizing
the staff report. She provided background on the property, noting that the lot is 10,856 square feet
with a 2,909 square foot residence. She explained the property has undergone various improvements
over the years, including a pool in 1974, a kitchen and family room remodel in 2010, and recent solar
panels in 2021.

Senior Planner Berry noted that the Planning Commission previously approved entitlements for the
property in December 2020, including a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination, Variance, and a
Minor Deviation for attached covered porches in the front and rear yards and a new balcony along
the rear elevation. The Variance allowed the property to exceed lot coverage by more than 10%, and
the Minor Deviation allowed the covered porch in the rear to be built along existing building lines. The
pool and patio areas were intended to be demolished; however, in preparation for the demolition the
owner discovered that the concrete patio was not done as anticipated and portions of the west edge
require a new retaining wall. The proposed improvements include a new 524 square foot rectilinear
pool and spa; 750 square foot. by right ADU; retaining walls; new concrete pathways and steps; and
grading to support the improvements.

Senior Planner Berry provided the results of staff’s assessment of the Neighborhood Compatibility
criteria. She noted that that the project conforms to five of the six criteria, and that the scale of the
project is not compatible due to the Variance request for increased lot coverage beyond what was
previously granted by the Planning Commission.

Senior Planner Berry explained that the Variances are to allow for a horse keeping area closer than
35 feet to dwellings; and to allow the property to exceed lot coverage by more than 10%. She noted
that the neighbors at 84 Dapplegray Lane provided a letter of support for the horse keeping area
variance. The homeowner’s association also supported the project given the substandard lot size.

Senior Planner Berry explained that in regard to the Grading Permit, discretionary review is required
due to fill greater than 3 feet in height and import of more than 20 cubic yards. She provided staff’s
assessment of the Grading Permit criteria and stated that they were met.

Senior Planner Berry noted staff received three comment letters: a letter of support from the
Dapplegray Lanes Property Owners Association and from 84 Dapplegray Lane, and a letter of
opposition from 80 Dapplegray Lane, expressing concerns about construction impacts.

Senior Planner Berry stated that staff recommended the Planning Commission open the public
hearing, take testimony, discuss the issues, close the public hearing, and adopt Resolution No. PA-
250001 approving the project.
Chair Olson opened the floor for questions from the Commission.

  2
Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
May 5, 2025
 Commissioner Yoo asked about the ADU's proximity to the horse keeping area. Ms. Berry clarified
that the ADU is not included in the lot coverage calculation per State ADU Law, which takes
precedence over the City’s requirements.

Chair Olson raised a philosophical question about whether irregularly shaped or undersized lots
should receive special allowance through variances. He asked whether it was appropriate to have an
expectation that variances will be granted when purchasing a substandard lot.

Commissioner Repp-Loadsman responded that variances are considered on a case-by-case basis.
She noted it would be unusual to grant a variance for a standard lot, but it can be considered for
unusual properties to find a reasonable balance. She added that approving variances does set some
precedent for similar properties.

The Commission discussed the proposed horse keeping area setback reduction from 35 feet to 19
feet. Chair Olson expressed concern about allowing horses so close to structures, citing issues of
odors, noise, and health impacts. He suggested exploring options to maintain the 35-foot setback.

Kelsey Fair, Project Designer, explained the challenges with relocating the horse keeping area due
to grading issues and impacts to neighbors. She emphasized the property is not practical for actual
horse keeping given its small size.

The Commission debated various options, including relocating the ADU and horse keeping area; the
size of the horse keeping area setback; removing the horse overlay designation from the property;
and adding deed restrictions.

Director Naughton provided clarification on code requirements and limitations regarding these
options.
Brian Little, property owner, spoke in support of the project. He explained they have worked to
improve the property and bring it into compliance since purchasing it 5 ½ years ago. He noted they
do not intend to keep horses on the property, and that horses have never been kept on the property
according to the DLPOA records.

The Planning Commissioners continued to discuss concerns about setting precedent by reducing the
horse keeping setback. Chair Olson suggested continuing the item to allow the applicant to revise
the site plan to comply with the 35-foot setback.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER REPP-
LOADSMAN to,

  CONTINUE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-250001 TO THE NEXT PLANNING
  COMMISSION MEETING.

AYES: Olson, Nicklas, Repp-Loadsman, Romanelli, Schachter, Yoo
NOES:
ABSENT: Medawar
ABSTAIN:

9.  COMMISSIONER ITEMS

Chair Olson thanked staff for the recent joint City Council/Planning Commission meeting, noting it
was productive in clearing up ongoing issues.

10.  DIRECTOR ITEMS

Director Naughton provided a preview on upcoming zoning code changes, which include:
  • ADU ordinance updates to address State law changes
  • SB 9 exemptions for H district properties
  • CalFire has distributed new Fire Severity Zone Maps and will require General Plan and Safety
  Element amendments
  • Landmark overlay ordinance improvements to strengthen protections for the city’s historic
  properties
  • Residential district standards updates will be based on analysis of past entitlements
